clue.text: Just like that thieving hearty rascal!

definitions.text: Just like that thieving hearty rascal!

parts.words: Just like that thieving hearty rascal
parts.note: the thieving rascal of hearts is the nursery-rhyme Knave of Hearts who stole the tarts; the clue asks for the adjective meaning 'like him'

explanation.surface: An exclamation about some cheerful, light-fingered rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearty' looks like a description of a jolly rogue, but it points to the suit of hearts: the Knave of Hearts in the nursery rhyme stole the tarts.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes behaviour like that of a dishonest rogue or scoundrel.

clue.text: One of 13 makes a record in King's Square

indicators.note: the record is placed inside the letters for the king's square

parts.note: in old descriptive chess notation the king's square is K1, here read with the 1 as I
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Someone joins a set of thirteen by setting a record at a royal square.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is FORAGE CAPS; 'King's Square' suggests a place, but it is the chess square K1, from old descriptive notation.
explanation.definitionFit: A kepi is a French military cap with a flat top and visor, a kind of forage cap.

clue.text: No, it takes a bird to give rise to liveliness

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the run of letters reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the mina, or myna, is an Asian starling

explanation.surface: Someone's claim that adding a bird produces liveliness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give rise' turns the whole run NO IT A MINA upwards, giving ANIM A TI ON; 'takes' and 'to' just join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation is vitality and spirit, being full of life.

clue.text: But this substance is not a metal as specified.

parts.note: taken as written
tin is a metallic element

explanation.surface: A chemist insists the substance is not a metal, despite what the label says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as specified' says the words spell it out: the substance 'is a tin', though it is not a metal at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Isatin is an orange-red organic compound, used in making dyes such as indigo derivatives.

clue.text: A measure of concealment?

definitions.meaning: an old English unit of land, enough to support a household
a hidden shelter for watching birds or game

explanation.surface: Asking how much secrecy someone is practising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A measure of' reads as 'an amount of', but it is a definition on its own: the old land unit.
explanation.definitionFit: An Anglo-Saxon land unit and a camouflaged shelter for observing wildlife share this word.

clue.text: A tribesman gave the doctor something to eat

parts.note: MO, Medical Officer, is a standard crossword doctor
a bite is a small amount of food, a snack

explanation.surface: A member of some tribe offered the medic a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A Moabite was a member of the ancient people of Moab, east of the Dead Sea, named in the Bible.

clue.text: Harmonicas brought round with the liqueur

indicators.note: bringing something round turns it about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Musicians pass harmonicas round along with the after-dinner drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Maraschino is a clear sweet cherry liqueur from the Dalmatian coast.

clue.text: "Violet, amaracus and " (Tennyson)

parts.note: a gap-fill quotation: the line from Tennyson's Oenone lists flowers, and the missing third is a lily of classical myth

explanation.surface: A line of Victorian poetry with its last word left blank.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's Oenone has 'Violet, amaracus, and asphodel'; amaracus is marjoram.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word names a lily-like flower said in Greek myth to cover the Elysian fields.

clue.text: But they don't make durance vile any smoother

definitions.text: But they don't make durance vile any smoother

parts.words: But they don't make durance vile any smoother
parts.note: 'durance vile' is harsh imprisonment; these shackles are also the household tools that smooth creases, yet they ease nothing for a prisoner

explanation.surface: A remark that fetters do nothing to make prison easier to bear.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word names leg shackles and the flat tools for pressing clothes: hence 'smoother'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetters of metal chained to a prisoner, and also laundry tools for pressing cloth.

clue.text: Gee! Fortissimo Uncle's turn shows brilliance

indicators.note: a turn is a change of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: ff is the musical marking for fortissimo, very loud
the word uncle, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: An exclamation at an uncle's loud, dazzling musical performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle's turn' reads as his go at performing; 'turn' is the anagram signal for GEE, FF and UNCLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Effulgence is radiant splendour, a shining light or brightness.

clue.text: Dine with Ralph? So Embarrassing — he will flirt!

indicators.note: an embarrassing situation throws things into disorder, so the letters of the two names are jumbled

explanation.surface: A diner warns about an awkward dinner date with Ralph, a known flirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two words of fodder; 'So' and 'he will' are surface padding before the verb 'flirt', which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To philander is to have casual love affairs, to womanise or trifle with affection.

clue.text: Evidence of having a pull with one's publisher

definitions.meaning: in printing, a pull is a trial impression taken for the author to check

explanation.surface: Showing that you have influence at your publishing house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a pull' reads as influence, but in printing a pull is a trial print sent for checking.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence that settles a question, and a printer's trial impression for correction, share the same word.

clue.text: Custom-built garment ?

definitions.meaning: a custom is a settled practice or routine
a robe such as a monk's or nun's, or a riding outfit

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing made to measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Custom-built' reads as one made-to-order adjective; split it and 'Custom' and 'garment' are both definitions, with 'built' a hint at the old sense of bodily constitution.
explanation.definitionFit: A routine practice and a religious robe or riding outfit are both called by this word.

clue.text: That's odd, Sue's " opal" wedding !

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name with its S, read as plain letters

explanation.surface: Sue is having an unusual opal-themed wedding, someone remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's odd' looks like a comment on the wedding, but 'odd' is the anagram signal: SUES plus OPAL rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Espousal is a formal word for marriage or betrothal, the act of taking a spouse.

clue.text: Top army veterans' wear ?

parts.note: 'Top' reads as senior, but is headgear; split the answer's first word and veterans wear caps meant for old age

explanation.surface: Asking what the most senior soldiers dress in.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as FOR AGE CAPS: caps for the aged, worn by veterans, and also the soldier's undress cap.
explanation.definitionFit: Forage caps are soft peaked military caps worn as undress uniform headgear.

clue.text: Sacking in the absence of the under-manager?

parts.note: Dis is the Roman ruler of the underworld, manager of what lies below
being missing is being absent

explanation.surface: Firing staff while the deputy manager is away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under-manager' reads as a junior boss, but is the god of the underworld, Dis; 'of' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismissing staff is firing them, giving them the sack.

clue.text: Chop the top of a leaf for this savoury dish

indicators.note: chopping off the top of a word removes its first letter

parts.note: a folio is a leaf of a book or manuscript

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: trim the tip of a leaf for the dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaf' suggests salad greens, but it is a page: FOLIO, which loses its first letter F.
explanation.definitionFit: An olio is a spicy Spanish or Portuguese stew, a hotchpotch of meat and vegetables.

clue.text: A time of greater illumination, lifting the load ?

parts.note: something giving more light is lighter
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: An era of more light, with something hoisted up.
explanation.walkthrough: A lighter is a flat barge used to unload ships, so lighterage is the work of taking a cargo off a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighterage is the transfer of cargo from a ship by barge, which lightens the vessel of its burden.

clue.text: It's in the middle, on the level

definitions.text: It's in the middle, on the level

parts.words: It's in the middle, on the level
parts.note: 'on the level' reads as honest, but refers to a spirit level, whose trapped pocket sits centred when a surface is flat

explanation.surface: A claim that something is centrally placed and above board.
explanation.definitionFit: A pocket of gas trapped in the liquid of a spirit level shows when a surface is true.

clue.text: Taught to find money in Chester's backwater

indicators.note: the money is placed inside the river's letters
the water is sent back, so the river's name is read backwards

parts.note: the city of Chester stands on the river Dee
a ducat was an old gold coin

explanation.surface: Learning to find cash in a quiet stretch of river at Chester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwater' suggests a stagnant creek; it turns Chester's river, DEE, backwards to EED, which wraps the old coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone educated has been schooled or instructed.

clue.text: Advancing years of a girl, nothing to do with skirt-length

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
O, the figure zero, means nothing
taken as written
a mini is a very short skirt length

explanation.surface: A woman's age is said to have no bearing on how short her skirts are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to do with' reads as one phrase meaning 'related to'; here DO is used as written, with 'to' and 'with' as joining words.
explanation.definitionFit: Anno Domini means 'in the year of our Lord', and is used informally for old age catching up.

clue.text: English schoolboy brought to book in America

indicators.note: the letters wanted sit inside the word America

explanation.surface: A British pupil finds himself published, or punished, in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought to book' suggests punishment; here it means put into a book: ERIC, or Little by Little, Dean Farrar's Victorian school story.
explanation.definitionFit: Farrar's 1858 novel follows a boy at a boarding school, the classic book-bound schoolboy.

clue.text: Eye droppers, improving one's sight

parts.note: 'Eye droppers' reads as medicine bottles, but means things that drop from the eyes; the saying is that these fall from one's eyes when the truth is seen

explanation.surface: Bottles of eye drops that help vision.
explanation.walkthrough: From the Bible (Acts 9): when Saul's sight was restored, 'there fell from his eyes as it had been' these.
explanation.definitionFit: Flakes said to fall from the eyes when someone suddenly sees the truth.

clue.text: You're out of spirits when he leaves

definitions.text: You're out of spirits when he leaves

parts.words: You're out of spirits when he leaves
parts.note: 'out of spirits' reads as gloomy or lacking drink, but means free of ghosts: once this cleric has done his work, the demons have gone

explanation.surface: A guest whose departure leaves you depressed, or with the drinks finished.
explanation.definitionFit: This person drives evil spirits out of a possessed person or haunted place.

clue.text: Beast is all right, to a good end

parts.note: OK means all right
pi, short for pious, means good

explanation.surface: An animal declared fine, coming to a good end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to a good end' reads as a happy ending; here A and PI (good) are added at the end of OK.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is an African mammal related to the giraffe, with a striped hindquarters.

clue.text: Pushing forwards

parts.note: reads as moving ahead, but means rugby forwards who are shoving against each other

explanation.surface: Advancing determinedly.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby, the forwards of both sides bind together and push in a set piece to win the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The rugby set piece where the two packs bind and shove for the ball.

clue.text: Dame made mead of it

indicators.note: made means remade, so the letters are rearranged; mead is a further rearrangement of the same letters

explanation.surface: A lady brewed honey wine from something.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame, made and mead are all rearrangements of the four letters of the cheese, which 'it' stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun stands for the Dutch cheese whose name the three words rearrange.

clue.text: The right conclusion? Tear, it up!

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
an end is a conclusion

explanation.surface: Someone, unhappy with the right ending, says to rip it up.
explanation.definitionFit: To rend is to tear apart violently.

clue.text: Girl with a small part to make suitable

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
pt is the abbreviation for part, so a small (shortened) part

explanation.surface: A young woman is given a minor role to fit her.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt is to modify something so that it fits a new purpose.

clue.text: A bill I need changed' can't be changed

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone needs a bill altered, yet it turns out to be fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'A' is a joining word, not fodder; 'changed' in the middle is the anagram signal, while 'can't be changed' at the end is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ink or a stain that is permanent cannot be removed or erased.

clue.text: A bit of leg to appreciate at a party !

parts.note: the shin is the front part of the lower leg
to dig is slang for to like or appreciate

explanation.surface: Admiring a glimpse of leg at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is a lively, noisy party or celebration.

clue.text: Deceive by playing the wrong card ?

definitions.meaning: to lead someone astray, to fool them
in card games, a lead is the first card played

explanation.surface: Fooling the table by laying down the incorrect card.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a false impression, and to make a poor opening play at cards, are the same word.
